items.title: Compare local OpenAPI contracts
acceptance: Capture bounded local JSON snapshots and compare them with the pinned real engine without changing source files.
Reject invalid or unsupported input instead of reporting an empty successful comparison.
Expose structural findings through SDK and CLI while marking consumer impact as not analyzed.
Verify the supported Windows, Linux, and macOS workflow and review the pull request.

items.title: Locate TypeScript consumers affected by contract changes
acceptance: Associate supported native HTTP call syntax with changed operations and local file/line evidence.
Report dynamic, ambiguous, or unsupported call forms as unresolved; do not imply exhaustive discovery.
Inspect consumer source without executing imports, installing its dependencies, or changing its files.
Exercise affected, unaffected, and unresolved usages with a fictional TypeScript consumer and its parser.

items.title: Preview explicit migrations against captured evidence
acceptance: Bind exact unique source edits to the consumer, contracts, recipe, and explicit business decisions.
Keep the consumer unchanged and unexecuted while showing reviewable before/after content.
Reject stale, ambiguous, overlapping, malformed, or out-of-scope recipes and expose missing decisions.
Prove the controlled call and parser transformation preserves the fictional consumer's internal model.

items.title: Propose and validate an authorized call and parser migration
acceptance: Bind a reviewable plan to source evidence, consumer revision, permitted files, and validation commands.
Require applicable authorization before mutation or consumer execution and use an isolated execution environment.
Demonstrate the consumer passing against version A, failing against B, and passing against B after the migration while preserving its internal contract.
Stop on ambiguous semantics or expanded scope and distinguish baseline failures from new regressions.

items.title: Persist local subscriptions and review jobs
acceptance: Persist exact bounded OpenAPI bytes and an explicit configured baseline without claiming adoption or deployment.
Observe local file subscriptions once, identify potential consumer impact, and retain pending review jobs across restarts.
Deduplicate identical evidence while preserving provider rollback transitions and changed consumer evidence.
Use expiring ownership claims and transactions so stale observers cannot commit; never grant approval or execute consumer code.

items.title: Resume authorized maintenance jobs
acceptance: Persist subscriptions, observed evidence, authorized jobs, and attempts without starting a worker on SDK import.
Reconcile interrupted validation, owned containers and late durable outcomes without replaying a consumed approval.
Respect changed source and consumer evidence, bounded ownership claims and authorization expiry.
Keep observed, validated, adopted, and deployed state distinct.

items.title: Publish an explicitly authorized migration from the customer environment
acceptance: Bind publication to a reviewed repository, base commit, remote destination, permitted files and validation evidence.
Require separate publication scope, isolate credentials from consumer execution and preserve human commits.
Create a branch and draft pull request directly from the local runner with idempotent reconciliation after uncertain responses.
Demonstrate the flow in an explicitly authorized test repository without automatic merge, deployment or code transmission to Keepseam Cloud.

items.title: Observe local MCP, schema, example and documentation evidence
acceptance: Compare the declared MCP and JSON Schema profiles with correct input/output direction; incomplete context cannot establish removal.
Persist immutable configured baselines, bounded snapshots and rollback transitions with transactional ownership and failure recovery.
Keep documentation and examples as evidence without inventing required fields, compatibility or execution authorization.
Expose public SDK and strict CLI entry points, with explicit limits and fictional examples.

items.title: Track version, boundary and dependency evidence locally
acceptance: Keep API, SDK, webhook and MCP versions separate, with source provenance, evidence for dates and unknown effective versions.
Register optional function metadata without wrapping or changing application behavior.
Inspect supported npm lockfiles and correlate provided exact-version advisories without executing package scripts or claiming exploitability.

items.title: Constrain customer-selected model proposals
acceptance: Bind selected context and adapter destination to explicit one-use consent; remote context requires an additional opt-in.
Enforce input/output/deadline limits and validate exact-edit recipes without editing selected tests or answering business decisions.
Preserve mandatory semantic review and separate model consent from execution and publication authorization.

items.title: Expose bounded scheduling and a private-data-free status contract
acceptance: Run finite explicit worker cycles with cooperative cancellation, no overlap and no automatic replay of failed execution.
Validate exact status wire shapes through keepseam-client/protocol, rejecting code, logs, prompts, schemas, commands and arbitrary labels.
Verify installed package imports, NodeNext types and CLI without import-time workers, database creation or networking.

items.title: Observe explicit HTTPS sources and inspect MCP consumer impact
acceptance: Capture explicitly allowed HTTPS URLs using scoped credentials, verified public addresses, pinned TLS connections and bounded responses.
Persist conditional cache, exact snapshots and successful observations atomically under ownership claims, preserving prior evidence on failure.
Migrate existing local databases without resetting baselines, pending jobs or execution history.
Associate declared MCP changes with explicitly bound calls and direct parser reads without executing customer code or granting permission.
Expose SDK and CLI flows with explicit network opt-in, cancellation and controlled local transport tests.

items.title: Operate persistent observation under native service managers
acceptance: Observe registered sources continuously with private state, singleton ownership, bounded logs and graceful cancellation.
Render explicit systemd, launchd and Windows SCM/WinSW definitions without installing services or downloading wrappers implicitly.
Exercise real observation, process loss, native recovery, stop and explicit restart on disposable Windows, Linux and macOS runners.
Keep execution, model disclosure, publication and package upgrades outside the observation service.

items.title: Install and configure the client without the development checkout
acceptance: Deliver an immutable private artifact with documented runtime, dependency and engine acquisition; require no access to the source repository or pre-populated developer cache.
Provide installed preflight and guided repository/source/test configuration, with explicit permissions and locally generated worker identity for existing Cloud enrollment.
Verify installation, observation, stop/restart and state preservation on a clean Linux x64 host; retain separate native Windows/macOS and validation-platform limits.

items.title: Turn observed provider changes into validated customer migration proposals
acceptance: Generate at least one supported migration through the installed client without requiring the customer to author an exact-edit recipe or model transport implementation for each job.
Connect impact, local plan approval, isolated baseline/candidate validation and separately authorized draft publication using the existing durable state and adapters.
Verify one real provider transition, then distinct SDK and MCP consumers; preserve internal call/parser contracts and stop on unresolved business assumptions.
Reconcile adoption against verified repository contents, preserve human edits and avoid duplicate migrations after process restart or repeated source observations; PR creation never means deployment.
Retain code, patches, private schemas and raw logs locally; Cloud receives only the approved versioned metadata contract.

items.title: Upgrade the worker independently from customer API integrations
acceptance: Verify explicit upgrades before offering opt-in automatic channels and maintenance windows; authenticate release artifacts and enforce metadata freshness and rollback policy.
Drain work, preserve credentials and durable state, check runtime/protocol/schema compatibility and verify health before resuming observations.
Exercise failed download, invalid artifact, incompatible state, crash during switch and compatible executable rollback without restoring stale approvals or losing outbox sequences.
Keep application-installed SDK updates as version-pinned repository changes; importing the SDK never updates running application dependencies.

items.title: Complete connected maintenance release gates
acceptance: Consume a versioned shared protocol in the separate cloud repository, including runner enrollment and revocation.
Provide the landing page, account onboarding, subscriptions, and dashboard with explicit runner availability.
Publish an authorized test PR directly from the customer environment and send permitted status updates to Cloud and Slack.
Demonstrate API and MCP scenarios without sending customer source, patches, raw logs, or private schema bodies to the SaaS.
